statusMessage:
Timed out after 902.244s.
The function passed to Eventually failed at /evetest/tests/upgrade/cluster_upgrade_test.go:191 with:
Unexpected error:
    <*fmt.wrapError | 0x3c70b29ee3a0>: 
    unable to reach app "6d2ac2a8-edc2-4144-9255-3e4a5c94a84c" SSH on device "edge-dev1": no reachable endpoint among [172.20.20.226:2222]
    {
        msg: "unable to reach app \"6d2ac2a8-edc2-4144-9255-3e4a5c94a84c\" SSH on device \"edge-dev1\": no reachable endpoint among [172.20.20.226:2222]",
        err: <*errors.errorString | 0x3c70b236e230>{
            s: "no reachable endpoint among [172.20.20.226:2222]",
        },
    }
occurred

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

Live inspection of `upgrade-app` (`6d2ac2a8-edc2-4144-9255-3e4a5c94a84c`) across all three nodes shows it's healthy, just not where the test is polling. On `edge-dev1` its `app-info` history ends in two consecutive `state:INITIAL` entries (no more BOOTING/RUNNING events after ~748236s), while `edge-dev3`'s `app-info` shows the same app reached `state:RUNNING` with pod IP `10.11.12.2` just afterward (`bootTime:1795748319`). This is the classic rolling-upgrade VMI eviction pattern: `edge-dev1` was cordoned/drained/rebooted for its baseos upgrade, the VMIRS evicted the app from it and rescheduled it onto `edge-dev3`, but the test's fixed SSH target (`cluster_upgrade_test.go:191`) kept polling `edge-dev1`'s `172.20.20.226:2222`, which genuinely has nothing listening for the app anymore — hence the 902s timeout.

This is the same mechanism already documented once before in the ledger under `TestThreeNodesUpgrade` (SSH-reach timeout against `edge-dev1:172.20.20.226:2222`, app actually relocated to `edge-dev2` in that case) — attributed there to a harness gap (fixed-device polling instead of resolving the node currently hosting a migrated app), similar to a recurring `FindDeviceHostingApp` bug seen for a different test. It is not one of the other previously-logged `TestThreeNodesUpgrade` failure modes (k3s single-node-bootstrap race, Proxmox `qmcreate` ZFS-lock timeout) — those have different signatures. Broker status shows the host at 105% memory overcommit but swap usage is low (0.5/8 GiB), so this doesn't look environment-driven tonight. No PR diff was supplied for this investigation.
